original_question: Let G be a hyperbolic group which is virtually compact special in the sense of Haglund–Wise. Suppose that the set of second Betti numbers of the finite-index subgroups of G is bounded. Must G be virtually either a free group or a surface group?
target_in_paper: The exact target is New Problem 21.139 in Unsolved Problems in Group Theory. The Kourovka Notebook: "Let G be a hyperbolic group which is virtually compact special in the sense of Haglund–Wise. Suppose that the set of second Betti numbers of the finite-index subgroups of G is bounded. Must G be virtually either a free group or a surface group?"
correct_elements: Your draft matches the paper’s official formulation essentially verbatim: it has the same class of groups (hyperbolic, virtually compact special in the sense of Haglund–Wise), the same boundedness hypothesis on second Betti numbers of finite-index subgroups, and the same conclusion asking whether G must be virtually free or virtually a surface group.
missing_details: To be fully stand-alone, specify what b_2 means, e.g. b_2(H) = dim_Q H_2(H; Q) for a finite-index subgroup H <= G.
Spell out the quantifier over subgroups explicitly: the boundedness concerns the set {b_2(H) : H <= G, [G:H] < infinity}.
Replace the informal phrase "is bounded" by an explicit equivalent statement such as: there exists C such that b_2(H) <= C for every finite-index subgroup H of G.
Make explicit that "virtually compact special" means that some finite-index subgroup of G is the fundamental group of a compact special cube complex in the sense of Haglund–Wise.
Clarify "surface group" as the fundamental group of a closed surface of negative Euler characteristic; in the hyperbolic setting this is the intended non-free surface case.
Optionally make the conclusion explicitly virtual: there exists a finite-index subgroup of G that is either a finitely generated free group or a closed hyperbolic surface group.
refined_question: Let G be a Gromov-hyperbolic group that is virtually compact special, meaning that some finite-index subgroup of G is the fundamental group of a compact special cube complex in the sense of Haglund–Wise. Assume that the set {b_2(H) = dim_Q H_2(H; Q) : H <= G, [G : H] < infinity} is bounded (equivalently, there exists C such that b_2(H) <= C for every finite-index subgroup H of G). Must G have a finite-index subgroup that is either a finitely generated free group or the fundamental group of a closed surface of negative Euler characteristic?
justification: The supplied arXiv identifier resolves to the Kourovka Notebook rather than to a research article with Conjecture 1.1, Proposition 1.2, and Theorem 1.3. The only substantive improvements are to make the problem self-contained by spelling out the meaning of the second Betti number, the finite-index quantifier, the boundedness condition, and the intended meanings of "virtually compact special" and "surface group."
